intro.title: Build typed plugin system
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed plugin system for a simple application. You will learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define a contract that all plugins must follow. This involves creating a plugin manager that can register and run different plugins while ensuring type safety. By the end, you'll understand how to structure a flexible, extensible system with strict type checking.
intro.usecase: Typed plugin systems are essential in modern applications where extensibility is required without compromising type safety. In developer tools like VS Code or Figma, plugins for syntax highlighting, linting rules, or design components rely on typed interfaces to ensure compatibility. Content management systems like WordPress use typed plugin architectures to safely extend functionality with custom blocks, widgets, and APIs. Even in enterprise dashboards, typed plugins allow teams to add custom charts, data sources, or authentication modules while maintaining reliable integration through TypeScript's type checking.
